utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before we move on, I'd like to deliver one decision from the Chamber and also make a statement on behalf of the Chamber. I will start with the decision, that is -- This is a decision on the Prosecution's request of the 9th of August, 2007 to make public two confidential annexes to a submission filed by Mr. Haradinaj on the 16th of July, 2007. On the 29th of June, 2007, Mr. Haradinaj requested temporary provisional release for the period of the summer recess. The Prosecution objected to this request on the 11th of July, 2007. On the 16th of July, Mr. Haradinaj filed a reply. Attached to this reply were two confidential annexes, containing a proposed public statement by Mr. Haradinaj and a letter by Mr. O'Reilly. The Prosecution now requests that these confidential annexes be made public. On the 20th of August, 2007, the Chamber was informed by the Defence for Mr. Haradinaj that it would not respond to the Prosecution's motion. Proceedings should be conducted, unless an exception is justified under the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, in public. Mr. Haradinaj does not object to the Prosecution's request. The Chamber sees no reason to keep the annexes confidential, and therefore, in the interest of the public character of the proceedings, grants the Prosecution's request. Mr. Haradinaj is ordered to re-file his 16th of July, 2007 reply as a fully public document but to redact, if he so wishes, Mr. O'Reilly's address, phone number, and e-mail address. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. The Chamber will now give a statement concerning the scheduling for the remaining part of the Prosecution's case. In this regard, the parties will have received the latest report from the Chamber's database, entitled "Report number 2," which indicates time spent on the case so far. After having heard the testimony of Witness 68 last week, the Prosecution had used up 107 of its 125 allocated hours. In reality, of course, the Prosecution has used a few hours more when you take into account Aleksandric, whose testimony has not yet -- has yet to be completed. The Prosecution has not requested any additional time for the presentation of its case. Considering how much time the Defence has taken for cross-examination and how much time has been spent on procedural matters so far, the Prosecution would require another 14 days, 14 hearing days, counting from the end of Witness 68's testimony, to complete its phase of the case. With the current sitting schedule, that would be the 8th of November. This being the case, the Chamber invites the Prosecution to file the remaining 92 bis and quarter motions, should there be any, no later than the 25th of October, 2007. The Chamber also invites the parties to formally announce by that date whether the Chamber can expect to receive any agreed facts, and if so, by when. So far the Chamber has not received any agreed facts. The Chamber also reminds the Prosecution that the statement of Jovanka Antic was provisionally admitted on the 22nd of May, 2007 pending the submission of a 92 bis attestation. The Chamber is not yet in receipt of this attestation, and the Prosecution should be aware that unless the Chamber receives it before the end of the Prosecution's case, the statement of Jovanka Antic will not be admitted into evidence. And this concludes the Chamber's statement on the scheduling for the remainder of the Prosecution's case. Mr. Emmerson, are you ready to continue the cross-examination of Mr. Stijovic [sic] -- no, no, we're still in chief. I apologise. Mr. Re, are you ready to --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, very much --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you said 15 minutes still to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's exactly what I said. While the witness is coming in, can I just add to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: At transcript page 9280 on Thursday, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you've got one second for me, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, I've -- I have a technical matter to discuss, first of all. There seems to be a --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There seems to be a problem with the -- with the live broadcast. We move into private session purely for technical reasons to see whether moving in and then out again will resolve the problem. It could not be excluded that it will. Therefore, Mr. Registrar, we'll move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I hear from the technicians whether this moving in and out has resolved the problem. I see the technician nodding "no." I do understand that the recording of the proceedings is functioning well. It's just the public broadcast, which as such is not a reason to suspend the proceedings at this moment, because the recorded hearing can be made available at a later stage to the public. Mr. Zivanovic, before we continue, I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, are you ready to continue your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, I am. The thing I -- there were two things I wished to mention first. One was at 9280 last Thursday, the 11th, I mentioned annexes 52, 57, 58, 60, 62, 75, and 88. They were all disclosed to the Defence on the 13th of February this year being attached to the witness's statement which were provided to them on that day. The second thing is I've asked -- we've asked the registrar to give a -- an MFI number to the index to the annexes, which I've circulated around, so that could possibly be tendered as an aide-memoire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be MFI ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be MFI P1102.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This is not evidence as such but just to assist us. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether this is an appropriate time to -- to argue matters of disclosure. I think not. I think, once again, they're -- the Prosecution's emphasis is misplaced between the issue of disclosure and the identifying of those exhibits and documents that they intend to put on their 65 ter list and intend to have as evidence as forms the basis of their case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I understood what Mr. Re just said just as an announcement of the days on which these documents were disclosed and not to --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's all, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to fully cover all the issues in relation to these documents. Mr. Re, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good afternoon again, Mr. Zivanovic. You may recall on Thursday afternoon we sent you away with some maps to mark on them. Have you been able to do that over the weekend?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Yes, I've done my homework; although, I seem to already have forgotten how this is done.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could perhaps I just have a look at these, just to see whether they need to be on the screen or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I -- I safely think we can rely upon these with an explanation from the witness and tender these into evidence. I think it would take too long to replicate it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps they can put -- be put on the ELMO. Would that assist?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then I suggest that later on they be uploaded in the e-court system that so that we have the -- the whole of the document available in electronic format as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The first one I -- I'm going to ask you about is in relation to the August offensive and which you refer to in your -- in your statement at paragraphs 98, 99, 100, 101, 102, and 103. And at paragraph 102 -- if that could just be briefly displayed in Sanction for a moment. You say that: "The combat group 3 assisted the MUP in taking Prilep from the KLA. You were present -- I'm sorry, I was present in Prilep with my units directing and controlling them and approving the decisions of the group commander. The MUP forces could not enter the village for two days because of resistance from the KLA and sought back-up assistance from a combat unit of the 15th Armoured Brigade, which entered behind the MUP units but through a different route." What we're interested in is the respective positions of the MUP and VJ and the KLA in that particular offensive. Have you marked those on that map which is now on the screen, or the ELMO? And can the ELMO please be displayed.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is marked on the map in blue, and this is the disposition of the Siptar terrorist forces here. In green I've marked the MUP forces. As you can see it in the key here. Red stands for the forces of the VJ supporting the MUP forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the -- in geographical terms, where did the VJ get to? What's the furthest point they got to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see, I mentioned here the dates 11 through the 13th, when these units I was superior to were active, and this combat group reached Rznic. It did not advance any further, as far as my unit is concerned. The MUP --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just a second. Just to pause there. The date the -- the date was 11th to 13th August, 1998; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the combat group you're referring to, is that the 3rd? That's BG-3?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Now, you were about to go to the MUP. Please explain.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. I didn't hear the interpretation that well. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said, "I did not -- sorry, it -- that's combat group 3, did not advance any further as far as my unit is concerned." Then you said "the MUP," and I interrupted you. And please tell the Trial Chamber where the MUP went.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ultimate objective was to enter the village of Glodjane and to search the area. The MUP entered the village of Glodjane and searched the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you see the Lake Radonjic canal area on that map? That's between Donji Ratis and the tip of the lake or the northern tip of the lake.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the canal. Neither I nor my units reached that area. It was the MUP that went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to rise to my feet, but I think that Mr. Re may have inadvertently misled the witness both by the question and by the witness's pointer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Our understanding is that the canal area is not the area that the witness then pointed to, nor the location that Mr. Re directed his attention to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say that the canal is longer than indicated by Mr. Re. It goes up to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Not -- not simply that, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I apologise. I was -- I was looking on the screen. That was the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's not Donji Ratis. I apologise. It's where it's marked "ZZ" and the -- and Stanka, that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness now pointed at where the parties would agree is the canal area. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is your answer the same, that your -- your units did not go down there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes., it's the same. I was present here in the canal area but in the vicinity of the village of Rznic. I merely observed the canal area from a distance to see what it was like. I didn't go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the concrete canal area? Are you aware of the area where the bodies were found?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you able to say how far from Rznic where the bodies were found?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't think --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Five to six kilometres. But I received the information from the superior command and the mass media. As I told you, I wasn't there on the spot, nor were my units.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That -- that does clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In light of the previous answer that the witness was not aware of the area where the bodies were found, he has now clarified the issue that from what he learned from the sources he mentioned, it would then be five to six kilometres. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar, that -- Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I've certainly no objection to that. I wonder if the witness might just be asked to clarify the legend which reads: "2.Od MUP," which he's written along the northern part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, close to the -- close to the lake where -- Your marking says: "2," apparently, "Od MUP," which is the marking closest to where the canal flows into the -- in Lake Radonjic. Could you tell us what that means.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This means the 2nd MUP Detachment, if I understand the question correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then further down where it reads "9.Od MUP," is that the 9th MUP Detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you're referring to what I'm just pointing at now, yes, that's the 9th MUP Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that you would like to know what that exactly means, Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Precisely which division of the MUP forces that involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us what -- you've heard the question by Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are special police units and the strength of the detachment is some three to four hundred men, sometimes less.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And finally, when the witness refers to "special police units," obviously we are aware of both the SAJ and the PJP, as well as potentially the JSO. I wonder if he can assist us to which of the special units he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] PJP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Re, first of all, Mr. Registrar, we need a number for this document, later to be uploaded in e-court, and that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be P1103.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I am not confident that the entirety of the markings that are on the map are exhibited on the ELMO. I'm not sure if that's the case or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we zoom out for a moment so that we see -- it may be that the dates, which I expect to be in the left upper corner -- and otherwise, perhaps, Madam Registrar -- Madam Usher, if you would -- yes, we see that there's the 11th until the 13th of August, 1998 written on top of the map. Could you move the map in such a way that we can see all the markings. Perhaps you start to the left-hand side. If you'll just move the map in such a way that we go through -- yes, that seems to be ... I think nothing further down, markings. Anything further to the right? No, that seems to give a complete picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My -- my question is -- and perhaps I've missed it, and perhaps if I did: On the left-hand side of the map, there is a -- a designation of "10.Od MUP," has that already been identified? Perhaps I missed that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But I take it that's the 10th Detachment. Would that be also PJP, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the units mentioned here in green and have to do with the MUP are PJP units.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry to keep --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- bobbing up and down. But since we're dealing with all the indications on this map. The witness has indicated as regards those deployments along the main road of VJ forces that they are forces of BG-3. I wonder if he can confirm whether or not BG-52 is in fact not a part of BG-3 but a part of the 52nd Military Police Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you confirm that, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This marked as "BG-3" is from the 125th Motorised Brigade. The other units are from other elements of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm so sorry, but specifically BG-52 is marked on the banks of Lake Radoniq. From other evidence, my expectation is that that would be a reference to the 52nd Military Police Battalion. I wonder if the witness could confirm that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's Combat Group 52 from the Pristina Corps. I don't see how else to regard this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's -- Mr. Emmerson is just seeking full understanding of your markings. Mr. Re -- oh, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I trust that we've dealt with all the markings on the map at this point now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I take it that we have. That's why I invited Mr. Re to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I've asked for it to be tendered -- I've asked for it to be tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes. And a number has been assigned. And is there any objection against? There's no objection. Then the marked map is admitted into evidence and it was P1103. Yes. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The other map you have there, Mr. Zivanovic, does that refer to the offensive described in paragraphs 130, 131, 132, 133, 134, 135, 136 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was in the month of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If it could just be displayed in Sanction for one moment, 135, so that it could be followed where I'm going, where you say --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You issued a combat order on the 8th of September, 1998 to Combat Group 2 to support MUP units in attacks against the KLA in the directions of Prilep-Rznic-Dasinovac-Donja Luka axis to capture Rznic. Combat 3 -- Group 3 was ordered to support the MUP units along the Suka-Crmljan-Donji Ratis axis and taking Grgoc village." Could that be -- the map on the ELMO please be displayed.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, here it is. Combat Group 2, supporting the MUP forces along Rznic, Grdaja, and on to Dasinovac. And this is Combat Group 3, which supports MUP forces along this axis, to Donji Ratis -- or rather, my unit reached the area of Krst Rakovica [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And just turning to the legend you have there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, for the record, the last location mentioned, Krst Rakovica appears on the map just north of the northern tip of Lake Radonjic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The legend there, it's in the bottom right-hand screen. It says "Legenda" -- you've got "STS," I can't read what the other two are. One's blue, red, and green. Is it the same as the legend on the earlier exhibit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's also a key, and this is trig 509, Krst Rakovica. Perhaps you can't see it on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I'm asking you about is the key to the red, green, and blue positions. Have you used the same colour scheme as you used on the map for August? Blue for the -- blue for the KLA?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, blue for the KLA; green for the MUP; and red for the VJ. The green arrows indicate the missions, how far the MUP forces were to advance with the support of the VJ. The same type of indication was used in the actual documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And are the green lines with arrows pointing from them, are they from -- are they the positions from where the VJ units started in the operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the green lines or semicircles or semi-spheres with an arrow. Behind them were the VJ units. The -- the military was never at the head of the advancing forces. It was always at the back ready to provide support where needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: To clarify too, in the top right-hand corner of what's displayed, it says: "BG-15-2," and there's a -- a red semicircle with an arrow next to -- in between two green lines, indicating MUP, with "5.Od," what's that one referring to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means these were the forces of the 5th Detachment of the PJP supported by the Combat Group 2 of the 215th Brigade of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And on the bottom right, to the left of the legend, near -- I think it says "Rakovina," there's a red line between a green arrow and a green one pointing towards two blue half circles just in the area of Maznice. Which unit was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you're referring to. Rakovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yeah, just where you are. Just there.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, this is a key which says what this line means: "VJ forces." That's part of the key of the legend.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Oh, I see. I see. Can you go to the left, please, to the left of the lake, and near Gramocelj there's a red line underneath two green ones. I can't read which unit you've placed there. Can you please tell us which one that is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should have had a black marker. I had a ball-point pen. This is BG-243-1, which means the combat group of the 243rd Mechanised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And on the main road above "Rastavica", to the left of this diagram, just above the road to Prilep, there's another red line with two green lines. Which unit is that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The green lines indicate the 1st MUP Detachment or the 1st PJP Detachment; whereas, the red line stands for the combat group number 2 of the 125th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How far did that particular unit go in those combat operations described on -- on this map?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the 125-2?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It came out to this line, which stands for the canal going on to Lake Radonjic. It did not go any further toward Dasinovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the blue lines, semicircular with little hatches on the top of them like crowns, like the one near Ljumbarda, what do they indicate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are detected positions of the Siptar terrorist forces that were fortified with shelters and an artillery system. This marking with an arrow stands for Papracane, where there was a barracks. And we had information that around 200 terrorists were present there who could intervene toward our left flank. This stands for "HQ," headquarters. We believe that there was a headquarters at Papracane and in the village of Ratis.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the one which is just to the left, lower left of Papracane. There's another one there, just above "Crnobreg." Which one does that refer to? I think it's just above "Beleg."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also a defence system that was set up by the Siptar terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can -- perhaps could we just scroll across the top to see whether there are any other markings on this document. You've marked it "8th to the 9th of September, 1998." Can you please just scroll to the left and right. Okay. Now the other way. And up. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: For purposes of clarification, in -- in both of the places where there is marking in red, there is on the red line both a square with a line and one of them has a diamond on it. Could we understand what that means. I think it might mean "motorised brigade." It might signify that. But I'm not sure. That would be up on the upper right-hand side near the Bandera, between those green lines. There is a box and a diamond shape in red.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you see that, Mr. Zivanovic? Just north-east of the other "Glodjane" there's this red line with a box and with a diamond-type of ... Could you tell us what that means.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, I will tell you. This means -- well, this diamond here means that this is a tank unit. And this part here means that it's a mechanised unit. And now, tank. I assume that you all know what a tank is. It is an armoured carrier, an APC, or a combat vehicle of the infantry. There are no other markings, not in this case. In this particular case, they all had something. Where there is nothing else, it means that it is pure infantry.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence too, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- yes, first there seem to be some questions before we move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Certainly no objection to it being received into evidence. I noticed that to the left or west side of the lake and immediately to the left of that -- of Donji Bites, the witness has marked the letters "SAJ." I'm assuming that that refers to the specialist anti-terrorist police group, the SAJ. What's not clear to me is whether that annotation relates only to the green line immediately above it or to any other of the formations that have been drawn in green, as distinct from PJP formations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic; you've heard the question. Could you please answer it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this part here is -- I mean, both pertain to the special anti-terrorist units, as Mr. Emmerson said just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that refers to the green bended lines, both just above "Gramocelj" and a little bit east of that, where "SAJ" is written. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And are we therefore to assume that all of the other green O-shaped lines refer to PJP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But I would kindly ask you to follow this. See, this is what the task of this unit was. See? That is one task, one assignment. And it involved these two green lines within the accomplishment of this assignment. See the rest? The arrows. All of it is drawn exactly what was supposed to be done by these two green lines, conditionally speaking. In these particular cases, it is the SAJ. And up here it is the PJP. Wherever it says "MUP Detachment," it is a PJP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When the witness referred to the arrows, he was referring to the five open arrows just north of the two bended green lines, SAJ. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And do the green arrows indicate the direction or the task that these units had?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could that receive an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes P1104.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there are no objections, then P1104 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The other document I wish to show you is 65 ter 1215, which is the overhead satellite map of the Dukagjini area, including Lake Glodjane -- sorry, Lake Radonjic. I just want to ask you: In general term, as a experienced military officer involved in the conflict there in 1998, and looking at the -- this map showing the geographical layout, to describe where the advantages lay to either side from the -- in the terrain, that is, including the populated areas, the mountainous areas, and the flatter areas, and the lake.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At any rate, the area that can be seen here, the satellite image, that is, it is my conclusion that it's the terrorists that prevailed, because they are on edges of the built-up areas, the settlements, and it is very hard to approach these areas without being very noticeable or without coming across some natural or manmade obstacles, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could we get a pen and the witness mark on that the areas where the terrorists had the -- or the advantage or prevailed, and the areas where the military would have had the advantage. Mark in -- before you mark, I want to use different colours. And if you could use blue for terrorists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm entirely in the Trial Chamber's hands as whether the questions and answers as framed are of any assistance. For my part, reviewing the record, the questions and answers put in that very general fashion, without time frame, without specifics, without events but simply as an overall assessment of the topography, are difficult to interpret and apply and of relatively limited usefulness. But it may be that -- I simply raise it at this stage so that if -- if an answer of clarity is sought, that the opportunity is there to seek it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Colonel Crosland gave a lot of evidence about terrorist and counter-terrorist actions and what the MUP were doing and what they should have been doing the way that, for example, control units were -- or check-points were placed on the roads, and so on, and the advantages that one had side had against another. I'm simply asking this witness in general terms and given -- given the time limitations, just to describe in general time -- in general terms in that period, because the geography doesn't change, as to where the natural advantages lay with one side or the other. That's as far as I take it. If I wished to do it, it would take a long time doing it plotting it month by month. I simply can't do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. At the same time, you also will understand that if it's done in a rather general way that, of course, it's more difficult to use that -- the answers for any conclusions. Let me just see ... Yes. You are mainly referring to the geographical features that would favour one or the other party. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Including -- including human -- sorry, including urban geography and physical geography.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness may answer the question. If you can do so. I take it that since the geography and since the populated areas did not -- although there may have been some movements, but there were villages, there were towns, that you take that into consideration for the whole of the period you were present.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I? I don't know what colour is active now. I need blue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Blue is active.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try. Yes, it is blue. Right. Thank you. Let me put a circle here, roughly what the advantage of the terrorists is. At this point in time, this is it. It's this part. Why? Because of the forest there in part. Then there's a settlement. Then also it is above the terrain that one crosses when approaching the area. And could I have red now, please. Is it there? Red? Now, what is suitable for the army in this case? This -- this part here and this other part, towards Erecka Suka. All the rest is not exactly amenable as far as the army is concerned or, rather, the MUP. That is what I have to say in response to this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Unless any further clarification is sought by my colleagues on the other side of the courtroom or by the Trial Chamber, I just ask that this be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be P1105.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Re. Then that's the number. No further clarifications. Any objections against admission? I see nodding "no" three times. Therefore -- therefore P1105 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to ask, if I may, for the Trial Chamber to take the break a little earlier than normal. I can make a start, but I would like to have an opportunity to briefly consult with my client --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- in the break on the evidence that has just been given, in particular the maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I have received a request to have the break at 3.30 in order to fix the broadcast issue. But may I take it that an earlier break would not be a problem? So I take it that rather not later than 3.30. Yes, that's well understood. Mr. Emmerson, we can have a break if not later than 3.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. You'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Emmerson, who's counsel for Mr. Haradinaj. Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, I just want to start, if I may, by understanding the testimony that you have given about the constitutional responsibility of the VJ and how that changed over the first half of 1998. You told us in your testimony last week that initially - and I'm looking here at page 9293, for those who are following - that initially under the Constitution it was the responsibility of the VJ to guard the border, including a 100-metre belt along the border, and that everything else was within the jurisdiction of the MUP. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, up to the month of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And then if we move to the month of May. And I am reading here from your 92 ter statement at paragraph 68. You say that in -- in May 1998, the Assembly of the FRY passed a law giving the military control over the area south of the Rozaj to Pec to Decani to Gjakova to Prizren to Dragash road and extending up to the border. You say it was approximately a 5-kilometre strip -- I apologise, a 5-kilometre belt or strip to the border. And I just want to understand that. First of all, do you remember now whether this occurred at the beginning of May, the middle of May, or the end of May, or roughly when in May it was that your constitutional responsibility expanded from 100 metres to the 5-kilometre belt you described?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the second half of May. I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When we look at the maps you've been marking and focusing in on the main Peja to Gjakova road in particular. As it appears on the map, we're speaking about the area to the west of that main road; is that correct? Between the main road and the border.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Okay. So until that point in time, in the second half of May, your area of -- was 100 metres. Then from the second half of May, it became a 5-kilometre strip to the west of the main road. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then you told us in your testimony last Thursday that in June the Supreme Defence Council authorised the VJ to become involved in anti- terrorist activities. This is page 9310 to 9312. And in particular, in answer to a question from Judge Orie, you said that: "Although no state of emergency had been declared, that from June 1998 the units of the VJ could be deployed to support the MUP forces in the anti-terrorism struggle," in your words. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. The Supreme Defence Council -- it's not that they approved it. They made a decision to use the army in support of MUP forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, again, can you help us as to when in June that occurred?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The end of June. I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for that basic instruction. I'm going to look in -- in some more detail with you at some of the deployments that occurred in that first half of the year and ask you to explain how they fit in with that framework, if I may. But, first of all, can I ask that you be handed out copies of a -- of a binder of documents which are going to be used in the course of cross-examination. Some of them, so that you understand, are documents that are already exhibits to your 92 ter statement. But for ease of reference, I've gathered them together into a single bundle for the purposes of cross-examination. Could you turn, please -- for the witness, Madam Usher, to tab 3 in the bundle. Tab 3 is Exhibit D168, and it is annex 9 to Mr. Zivanovic's 92 ter statement and is the document of the 27th of April, which Mr. Re asked some questions about last week. If you could turn to tab 3, please, and to paragraph 5, where there is a record of the contact that took place between your officials from the 125th and the special unit under the command of Frenki Simatovic that was deployed at around that time to Deqan and Istog. I just want to understand your evidence in relation to this correctly, if I can. You told us last Thursday that this unit was a unit of the JSO. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you said their task was to find out precisely where the illegal border crossings were in order to enable other forces to prevent those crossings. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and larger groups, in terms of illegal crossings.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So presumably it must follow that if they were going to assist in identifying where crossings were taking place so that other forces could prevent them, there must have been some liaison established between that unit and your unit, whose task it was to prevent those crossings from occurring. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry. It's not quite correct, and I did not have any liaison with them and they did not provide for such liaison. We could react within a 100-metre belt and it was only after the 2nd of May that we could react within a 5-kilometre belt.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. But let me just read to you the testimony you gave last Thursday about this grouping. You said: "Their task at the time, which was late April, May, and June, was to find out exactly where the illegal border crossings were taking place in order for all the other forces to be engaged in preventing these crossings." Now, you've already told us that your primary function was to patrol the border. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And to prevent illegal border crossings.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we cannot do within 100 metres, then we have the MUP forces engaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that, but you're describing here a task performed by this unit in April, May, and June, at a time when, as you've told us, the VJ's area of responsibility moved from 100 metres to a 5-kilometre belt. And what I'm trying to understand is how would that unit convey to your forces the exact positions where illegal border crossings were taking place and how would your unit then respond in preventing them if there wasn't some form of regular liaison between you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps we are not understanding each other. When I say that they detect them, that means that then they take action as well. And then there's a different matter: If they notice this and if they feel the need to convey that to the military units there, then they would convey that to the ministry and then it would come down the corps communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So if information was conveyed to the 125th, it was conveyed via the ministry rather than directly between this JSA -- JSO unit and your officials; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. So not through direct contact. Not through the ministry for me. For me it is my corps commander that mattered. He conveyed information to me and members of his command.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: See, this document which you -- bears your signature, Mr. Zivanovic, it refers to this group as "the so-called Frenkijevci," which if I've understood correctly, is Frenki's Boys. Is that a correct translation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. Up until that time, I didn't even know who and what these Frenkijevci, Frenki's Boys were.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Presumably, though, at the time you wrote this report, you'd understood what the term "Frenki's Boys" had come to mean, because you refer to it as "the so-called Frenki's Boys"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. I found out then that I was supposed to establish communication with Frenki's Boys. Who they were, what they were I found out only later.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So having established communication on one occasion, you then cut it off from that point onwards; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When I felt it was necessary to communicate with them, then I reported to my corps commander, who enabled this contact. So then I would go there or I would receive a person from that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that's what I wanted to be clear about. So you -- you would visit them and they would visit you. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that I followed some of their activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, can I just seek some clarification on that answer as well, because you told us in your evidence last Thursday that you saw them on three occasions in July and August in active combat in the Drenice region on three separate days. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in July and August all three times. In Drenica, near the Devic monastery, for the most part. And then once from Decani to Voksek along the road of the Decani brook towards the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When Mr. Re in your in evidence chief last Thursday showed you a document dated the 8th of August which referred to the Brazil Group and their involvement in a wedging and burning operation, what was the relationship, if any, as you understood it, between the Brazil Group and the JSO based at Deqani and Istog?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you an exact answer with regard to that. Actually, I can tell you that the JSO did not work -- I mean, they just coordinated things, but I don't know who they got their tasks from.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But the Brazil Group that you referred to in the document on the 8th of August, the Brazil Group is part of the JSO, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's a special anti-terrorist unit of the MUP. I already said that, a special anti-terrorist group. SAJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So just look behind tab 2 in this volume, at that document of the 8th of August, just before we break. Mr. Re took you on Thursday to the entry that refers under paragraph 1.2 to the Brazil Group carrying out deep-wedging and burning operations. Could I ask you, please, to look at the very last three lines of the document under tab -- under paragraph 4. This is D165 we're referring to, for the sake of the record. And in the English translation it reads: "Troops in PJP units, particularly the 3rd and 7th PJP Detachments, are not well trained, while JSO, particularly the Brazil Group, are very well trained for conducts of all b/d, particularly to protect our b/v," combat vehicles. You refer, don't you, Mr. Zivanovic, in this very document to the fact that the Brazil group are a constituent part of the JSO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This "O" was probably added, but it's special units. You know, sometimes mistakes are made in the Morse code when one uses that form of communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So where -- just to be absolutely -- does the original say "JSO"? Could you just read, please, the last three lines of the original document for us from the word "dok su." Could you read it aloud for us so that we can have a translation, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry. I'm just trying to find the context. I'm trying to find the section that you've referred me to. It's at the very end, you say. "One of the main problems is the cooperation between the MUP and our combat vehicles, because members of the MUP are not trained for acting in concert with combat vehicles and also there is fear from possible consequences. In the case of PJPs, especially the 3rd and 7th Detachment of the PJP, the manpower haven't been trained properly, while the units of the JSO, especially Brazil Group, are very well trained for carrying out all combat activity, especially in protecting our combat vehicles." I am telling you the Brazil is SAJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Would that be a convenient moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I said yes, that's a convenient moment. Before we have a break, Mr. Zivanovic, there was some other homework we invited you to do, that is, to re-draft the wedging and burning operations with colours. I don't know whether you managed to do that. You may have forgotten about it. It was not as explicit as ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry, but you weren't very specific or unequivocal when giving me that task. I did do something, and I hope that will be right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you'd give it to Madam Usher, then the parties will have a look at it and see whether it assists. We'll have a break until 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, I want to come back just to an answer you gave shortly before the break. When you said in relation to this JSO contingent stationed near Deqani, you said: "When I felt it was necessary to communicate with them, then I reported to my corps commander, who enabled this contact. So then I would go there or I would receive a person from that unit." Can I ask you, please: Between the 27th of April and the middle of the year, how frequent were those contacts?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're referring to the middle of the year, end of June, then there were two contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And who did you understand, then, to be in command of that detachment of JSO officers in Deqan?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will give you his name. He was Colonel Rajo Bozovic, a colonel in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You say "a colonel in the police." Do you mean a colonel in the regular MUP forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really understand this division between State Security and the police that well. To me that's all Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the -- the British military attache to Belgrade, Colonel Crosland, is that a gentleman that you came across from time to time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He has testified in this case and has produced a number of his daily situation reports. Now, I don't call them up at this stage, but in a report dated the 1st of June - that is, for the record, Exhibit P96 - he records the VJ barracks in Pec, as, to use his words "brimming with MUP," and saying that as he passed the barracks in Pec, he saw a JSO camouflaged communication vehicle inside the VJ barracks and a MUP helicopter. Can you help us about that? Were there contacts, then, with JSO communication vehicles attending the Pec barracks at the beginning of June?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a bit arbitrary to say that the barracks were brimming with MUP. It's true that in Kosovo in every barracks there was a building set aside for the police. The helicopter or a military helicopter could only land in a clearing, where normally the units fall in line. As for the communications, I can't really say that with any certainty. Normally where there are barracks, then the communication that is provided is wire communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Just to be clear, it -- the record is of a JSO camouflaged communications vehicle being located within the VJ barracks in Pec. Can you comment on that at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. I don't know what "camouflaged" means. We are in the military also had camouflaged vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. So, again, to be clear, were there visits by JSO at the beginning of June to your barracks, so far as you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. He also has filed or filed a report on the 13th of July, which again, for the record, is D76, in which he describes 150 JSO driving around Pec and seeing JSO officers openly drinking close to the VJ barracks. Do you -- do you recall seeing the presence of JSO officers driving openly around Pec in the middle of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't claim that with any certainty. Whether they were the JSO, PJP, or SAJ, they had similar uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you notice amongst the MUP officers evidence of them drinking alcohol close to barracks?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that with any certainty. I wasn't dealing with these problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, who to your knowledge is Milorad Ulemek, also known as Milorad Lukovic, also known as Legija?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Is it important?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Please. If you could just explain to us what his role was, as far as you understood it, in Western Kosovo in 1998.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that he was the commander of the unit for special operations. But what his role was is a question you should put to somebody from State Security when they come to testify here. I am not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. We'll come to that in a moment. But when you say "the unit for special operations," here, are you referring to the JSO or the SAJ?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: JSO.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you look behind tab 7, please, for a moment. This is a translation, first in B/C/S and then in English, of a letter written by Colonel General Perisic to Mr. Milosevic on the 23rd of July. And I just want to ask you about whether you can shed any light on two passages in this letter. First of all, if you could find point 3(a), that is 3, little (a), please. The English translation reads as follows: "Constant aspirations by members of the MUP to have some VJ units subordinated to them leads to misunderstandings if the units are not given, and if they are given, this represents unauthorised and unprofessional use which has counter-effects, the best examples being Decani and Orahovac." Now, pausing there for a moment. Deqani on the 23rd of July was within your area of responsibility, was it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was a peacetime area which entailed quite some other matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, can you help us, please. Do you know what Colonel General Perisic is referring to there when he says that "there have been attempts by the MUP to have VJ units subordinated to them" in July or by July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I know that I was never given an assignment to re-subordinate a unit to the MUP, nor did I give -- nor was I given an assignment the other way around, for a MUP unit to be re-subordinated to me. There was the planning of coordinated action; whereas, commanding was always a separate matter. There was the commanding over the MUP and over the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think -- I think we probably all understand the difference between coordination and subordination. But this letter is referring quite specifically to subordination of VJ units to the MUP and gives an example of a situation in which VJ units have been given which you -- represents unauthorised and unprofessional use which has counter-effects, and the best examples of that include Deqani. Can you help us, please, from your recollections as to what General Colonel Perisic might have been referring to as "unauthorised unprofessional use with counter-effects in Decani" of the subordination of VJ units to the MUP.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't help you there. I've been thinking about it now, and I did not have such a case involving my units. I can't tell you what Perisic had in mind when thus referring to Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you at this stage reporting to Perisic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, Perisic was the Chief of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia. In case he called me directly, I would have the obligation to execute the order, but this did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We've heard testimony from Colonel Crosland that on the 28th of July - so five days after this letter was written - he came across a joint strike force poised to launch a strike on Malisevo, which included VJ, JSO, and PJP officers, all of them commanded by Milorad Ulemek or Legija. Can you help us with that at all? Was there an occasion at the end of July where you subordinated forces to Milorad Ulemek as the overcall commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. Malisevo is not in my area and I can't tell you anything about Malisevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We'll come to your deployments in that area a little later on. For the record, it's 3048 to 3050 and 3094 in the testimony of Colonel Crosland?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Emmerson, should this document which --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and according to your list has not yet been MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could it be MFI'd. It's Defence document 1D64-0001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours that will be marked for identification as D179.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One additional question, Mr. Emmerson, if you would allow me. You -- I'm not a native speaker.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Whenever Your Honour says that, I generally find that I'm the one who's in the wrong, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's not anticipate on how you learn -- how to understand the English language. Mr. Emmerson, when I read 3(a) --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and it seems in your line of questioning you interpreted that in a very special way. It says "constant aspirations by members of the MUP to have some VJ units subordinated to them leads, A, to misunderstandings if the units are not given.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if they are given, it leads to unauthorised and unprofessional use which has counter-effects. And it said the best examples, in the plural, being this and this. So there are two options; either you give it or you don't give it. So one of the examples exclusively referred to the second option is linguistically not clear for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I take Your Honour's point. And on this particular occasion - and it may be a matter of linguistics - but on this particular occasion, certainly as -- as I read it naturally, if the examples intended -- were intended to be examples of a situation in which units were not given, they would appear after the first comma rather than after the second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or examples of both situations. For example, Decani, for the one situation, or Orahovac for the other one. But I just -- I just wondered whether my -- whether that is a reading which for linguistic reasons should be excluded, because you ignored it more or less in the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I take Your Honour's point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe that the comma qualifies the second -- would qualify the second phrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the issue, yes. That's the issue, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can -- it is a matter of, I think, from my point of view, the natural reading of the sentence. But I take Your Honour's point, but it's a translation in any event, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's another problem. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although, I certainly do not exclude that your reading of it would be right or -- but I'm just --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- ask myself whether it could be excluded to read it another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me just see if I can just cover both options.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was there an occasion, Mr. Zivanovic, when you were asked to subordinate VJ forces to the MUP but refused to do so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Such a request or order was never given to me by the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Colonel Crosland has also testified that he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, this answer is not unambiguous. You said never an order was given to you by the corps commander. The question is whether anyone ever tried to achieve a situation in which VJ units would be subordinated to MUP units. So apart from what the corps commander told you or did not tell you to do, was there any attempt in that direction as far as you know? By whomever.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I know is that there were no such demands or attempts to influence my position. And I am not allowed to do anything without the approval of the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Colonel Crosland has also testified that on a number of occasions in Western Kosovo during 1998 he saw VJ vehicles that had been re-painted so as their -- to appear blue and re-allocated to the MUP. Can you help us with that? Were there occasions within your brigade when VJ equipment was painted blue and provided to the MUP so as to appear to be part of an anti-terrorist operation, rather than a military operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can help you further with this matter in this way: The Pristina Corps did not give its assets to the MUP to use them. This was done at the state level in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So would it be the position, then, that there would be VJ equipment painted blue but that would have been authorised from Belgrade rather than at the level of your command? Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have a truck painted in blue, then this is an asset of the MUP, regardless of whether it was also used by the VJ. It is true, admittedly, that the VJ gave some of its -- some of its assets, but it was decided in Belgrade and then went down the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Whilst we are on this document and lines of command, if we look, please, to paragraph 4 - correct me if I'm wrong - but there is what appears to be a complaint by General Perisic that President Milosevic is bypassing the chain of command within the VJ. It reads as follows: "Passing over command levels in official conversations with VJ members; according to VJ Service regulations, you" -- that is, President Milosevic -- "have the right to conduct official conversations with all members of the VJ. However, you sometimes do this without the knowledge of the Chief of the General Staff, which is contrary to military subordination and unity of command. Violation of these principles leads to the break-up of the unity of the VJ." Now, pausing there for a moment. Colonel Crosland has testified in this court that he had conversations with General Perisic and with General Dimitrijevic at around this time in which they told him that they were being cut out of the chain of command because they disagreed with what had been happening over the summer in Kosovo and were not prepared to go along with the use of VJ forces in operations that involved the disproportionate destruction of civilian property. This is transcript 3062, line 15 and following. And Colonel Crosland testified that General Perisic and General Dimitrijevic told him that there was a direct line of command being established between Major General Pavkovic and Mr. Milosevic which excluded them and excluded General Perisic as Chief of the General Staff. Now, can you help us, were you aware that General Perisic was expressing concerns that he was being bypassed in the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that, because I was in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. As far as I'm able to see, this is correspondence between the President and the Chief of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to ask you, if I can, please, to help us just to identify some vehicles, and I want to play you a short piece of film, the transcript for which is behind tab 30(b). And this piece of film shows the MUP operation in the aftermath of events in Prekaze on the 5th of March. What I want to do is just to let you know what you're going to see is to look at the vehicles that are shown in this piece of film and help us, if you can, to identify them. And so that you understand what to expect, you will see an armoured vehicle involved in the destruction of a house, followed by a shot of two other pieces of heavy equipment. And I want you just to help us, if you can, to identify them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think we have a technical difficulty with the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear some text spoken. I do not see any image. And could I also ask our interpreters to follow the usual, that if there's any -- if it goes too quickly to translate into French, that one reads the transcript. Are the booths provided with the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that the other interpreter, even if a little bit behind from that transcript, translate.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's tab 30(b) for the assistance of the booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And 30(b) is not yet --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It is not yet marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we first mark 30(b) for identification. Mr. Registrar, that would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be document ID 1D36-0019. And it will be marked for identification as D180.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Let's hope that we get the images of the BBC News as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: The Serbs say their security operation is over but for the Albanians in Drenice the terror continues. The Security forces claim to have destroyed the core of the outlawed Kosovo Liberation Army, killing the group's leader and these did appear to be mopping-up operations. The homes of suspected KLA members are burned or bulldozed by armoured vehicles as both a punishment and a warning to the rest of the village. The Serbs say they are fighting terrorism but there is no military necessity for this. Scenes like these will bring more international condemnation of Belgrade. The only way into these villages is across country through the Serbian lines. Our cameraman was fired on. He was hit. A mobile phone and a money clip probably saved his life. Many of the villages in Drenice are deserted. People have obviously left in a hurry. It's not clear if they fled or were forced out, but the main ethnic Albanian political party has accused the Serbs of carrying out a new campaign of ethnic cleansing. Refugees are still leaving the area. Many families have been forced to spend the night in the hills. "We have to run away," she says. "It's war here. People are being killed, even children, and nobody does anything." The Kosovo Liberation Army says its members living abroad are returning here to join the struggle against the Serbs. There have also been expressions of sympathy from Albania itself and from ethnic Albanians in neighbouring Macedonia. This highlights what Western governments fear most, that continuing violence in Kosovo could destabilise the whole region. Paul Wood, BBC news, Drenice, Central Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I note that it's received an MFI number. I'm just asking: Is the Defence attempting to tender the transcript which contains an awful lot of opinion by the BBC journalist as truth of the matters therein asserted or as a general commentary on some BBC film footage?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, at the moment I'm tendering the transcript, because that's the procedure that we've adopted for identifying video material. I'm going to ask the witness some questions about the passage that we've just seen, and in particular, as I indicated before, the vehicles that were involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, we saw in that piece of film three heavy vehicles, one of which, as we saw, was demolishing a building and two of which were in the field. You can see now a still of the two that are in the field. The top vehicle appears to have Caterpillar tracks. Can you help us as to what those vehicles are?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you make the image a bit better? And I'm actually wondering whether it's a tank or an armoured combat vehicle. Can you zoom in a bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We can't, I don't think, zoom in on the video. We can play it again so that you can see the vehicles moving, just that short passage.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by what I can see here, this is an APC, normally carrying nine to ten men.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. That is the vehicle involved in the destruction of the building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a vehicle transporting men from position to position in order to protect them from infantry fire, and it has a 20-millimetre gun mounted on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you'd just play that short passage with the vehicles in again, please. And you can help us as far as you can with the identification of the vehicles involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just run it through. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, are you able to help us at all as to whether there are main battle tanks involved in that operation, from what you can see on that video?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't help you with that. This is only one footage, and it can be made anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But -- never mind where it's made. I'm simply asking you if you can assist with identifying the vehicles. And is the answer to that question that you can't?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Emmerson. As I said, this can be filmed during an exercise of the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you could focus just for a second on the question that I'm asking you. Never mind where it was filmed. The question that I'm putting to you is: Do you know what the vehicles are and to which force they belong? Now, you used the word "military" a moment ago, "an exercise of the military." Do any of those vehicles appear to you to be VJ vehicles?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this footage - and it is quite blurred, the image. I don't want you to misunderstand me - the vehicle was filmed from the rear end and on the basis of what I can see here, this is the combat vehicle of the infantry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The infantry of which force? The MUP or the -- or the VJ?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both had it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And can I ask you this: Did you yourself authorise or witness that type of property destruction in the aftermath of military operations where vehicles were used to destroy houses in that way?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question, I'm afraid. Can you please clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you yourself ever authorise or observe forces of the VJ or of the MUP using heavy vehicles to destroy Albanian properties in the way we see depicted in that piece of film?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I observed that, but only if the building concerned was a military target, because it was occupied by terrorists or because fire was opened from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So after an operation had concluded, would there then be a destructive phase in which buildings would be destroyed like that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, it strikes me that you do rely to some extent on the opinion given by the journalist. You are referring to it as after -- that's not visible from the images itself. Neither is it that these are places where civilians are living. I mean, there was no objection. But, of course, Mr. Re earlier said, for what reasons? Then you said, "I'd like to ask a few questions about the images."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is what you did. But you intertwingled -- intertwined with that part of the -- of the opinion commentary of the journalist. I -- just for you to know that I am aware of that and that would certainly be better to refrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The -- the Prosecution is also aware of it. And it was clearly apparent from the questioning and the answering. But we certainly want to know when this was taken and where it was taken. It's not apparent from the footage or the -- or the commentary.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I think it is -- I think it is tolerably apparent from the commentary, if I may say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: But where? Which village? Where? When? Town? Village?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It was in fact --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Roadside?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It was in fact an incident that was videoed in the immediate aftermath of Prekaze on the 5th of March. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what Mr. Emmerson said before, that he would show some pictures of that. But I do understand that Mr. Re would like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to know the reasons why you consider this to be a footage taken at that time, at that place.
