utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I -- I'm very happy to communicate the position with Mr. Re, if I may. It's not -- it's not the identification of it as being Prekaze as opposed to Drenice is not apparent from the transcript. I accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to turn, if I may, to some of the evidence that you've given and documents you've produced about VJ positions in the first half of 1998, and in particular VJ positions in the area to the east of the main Pec to Gjakova road. In your 92 ter statement at paragraph 8, you indicate that the military police battalion was stationed at a filtration plant at the southern end of Lake Radoniq. That's the 52nd Military Police Battalion. Can I understand, please, from where -- from what point in 1998 was the 52nd Military Police Battalion stationed at that location?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly from what point in time. And it's not only that it was positioned there, we were also engaged in mobile camping in March and April.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, could you explain what "mobile camping" means in this context.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means exercising everything that was learned up to a given point in time and blending it all together out in the field, in accordance with the curriculum taught.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that's helpful. Specifically, I am inquiring about the location of the 52nd Military Police Battalion and asking for some clarification of your witness statement at paragraph 8, where you say that -- that that battalion was posted at the filtration plant at the southern end of Lake Radoniq. Now, do I understand the position to be that that -- that was a mobile operation or -- or that the 52nd Military Police Battalion were posted there continuously? And if so, from when?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that I saw it there twice; that is to say, on two successive days. Now, whether it was there all the time, I cannot say with any degree of certainty, because it's not my unit. It is a unit that is commanded by the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And -- and, again, for the assistance of the Trial Chamber, on the two occasions that you saw it based there -- or I'm sorry, that you saw it stationed there, when were they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was sometime on the 7th or 8th of May, 1998, when I was transferring my own unit, which was also involved in training, from the village of Bec, the area of the village of Bec, to the barracks in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And just to come back to the expression you used a moment ago, "mobile camping." Where were your units engaged in mobile camping during March and April?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Combat Group 2, on the Pec-Klina road, Kramovik-Bec-Djakovica-Morina, that axis. Combat Group 1, in the broader area of Kosovska Mitrovica. I don't think that it really matters as far as this trial is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you could just turn, please, behind tab 1. There is a map there which was marked by General -- sorry, Colonel Bozidar Delic in the Milosevic trial which bears a legend which is behind tab 1B, indicating that it relates to deployments between the 22nd of April and the 10th of September. For the sake of the transcript, this is Exhibit D42. And we can see there that Mr. Delic has marked three areas in red on the terrain surrounding Lake Radoniq: One with a flag to the bottom right or south-east; one semicircle just beneath the "B" of Boka; and a further flag on Donji Bites with a figure "6" in it. Can you help us to -- with those deployments, please, and what they signify.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since this is colleague Delic's zone, then it was his right to mark that and to indicate this to you or to whoever. You asked about the south-east, the little flag. That is the 52nd Battalion of the military police. And as for the west -- you interrupted me. Did you want to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm simply thanking you for the clarification.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the area of the village of Bites, I see that it is an interrupted line, so I'm not sure what it is. He should have said so in the key. Does it have to do with the 52nd Battalion or some other unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think the key makes it clear that these are VJ deployments. I wonder if you could help us interpret the marking.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry, but I don't really have a translation of the key into Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put it to you this way, Mr. Zivanovic: Were you aware of VJ forces being stationed on Donji -- were you aware of --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's simply a larger version of the other map. Were you aware of VJ forces being stationed on Donji Bites? And if so, from what date?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not sure about Donji Bites. That is why I am asking for clarification. What this interrupted red line means within the red circle in the area of Donji Bites. It is customary that if there is an interrupted line, then this is an area that is yet to be entered.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you, then, from your own knowledge about deployments in this area, if I may. First of all, if we could just look, please, behind tab 8 in the green file, which you describe in your witness statement at paragraph 62. Tab 8 is Exhibit P1023, marked for identification with this witness, and is annex 5 to the 92 ter statement. If we could look, please, at, in the -- in the B/C/S, the second page under figure "2" and in the English at page 3 under figure "2". This document is dated the 24th of April and is signed by Colonel Lazarevic. And in paragraph 2, it identifies various deployments: "The schedule and tasks of all the units stand as previously organised, with the exception of BG-2 of the 125th Motorised Brigade, which was redeployed to the Boka sector during the day (one kilometre south-east from Kramovik village) and issued with the following task: "Take control of the axes Kramovik village to Kramovik ravine and Rakovina village to Djakovica. "Break up and destroy the DTG in Crmljane village and; "Secure the right flank of the 52nd bVP and fire at enemy forces along the axis Crmljane village to Rakoc village." Now, in your witness statement you indicate that BG-2 was based in Gjakova until the end of May. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the 23rd of May, when they went to the village of Ponosevac; that is to say, the area of the Morina border post.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so here on the 24th of April, do I understand that the whole of BG-2 is being redeployed to the Boka sector or a part of it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would kindly ask for -- for time for a broader explanation. When I said "mobile camping," I mentioned Kramovik as an axis. Kramovik was always well known as our training ground. And when one engages in mobile camping, then units are issued with tasks that resemble wartime tasks, so that command of units and preparation of units would be taught and learned. You see that these tasks are only on paper. They were not actually carried out in practice, in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So when a unit is tasked to break up and destroy the terrorist group in Crmljane and to secure the right flank of the 52nd Military Police Battalion, that was, what, an exercise on paper only?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As a small-scale staff wartime training in order to train commanders and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were the soldiers physically deployed or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The complete unit was in the Boka area; that is, this area of Kramovik. And they did not enter a single village or town except for Klanica Bec, where they were stationed later.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just to be clear, when they're tasked to engage in military action against the DTG, is that a serious order? Were they intended to in fact engage in military action against the DTG?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to understand this as a staff wartime exercise, and then it will be readily understandable to you that we are just exercising this particular action. We did not engage in any actual combat as far as this is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, you see, in your witness statement at paragraph 62, when you comment on this document, you say that "BG-2 was tasked with controlling the axis from Kramovik village to Kramovik ravine and Rakovina village to Djakovica," and you say "the aim was to break up the KLA forces in Crmljane village."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It primarily means observation, this word "controlling." Since you assist on active action, I am telling you that that was not the case. We did not actually enter these settlements. This was just on paper, fictitious.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so when it says in the order and in your statement that the BG-2 are to fire at enemy forces along the axis from Crmljane to Rakoc, that is an order you never intended to be carried into effect; is that right? Is that how we're to understand it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. This order was not carried out. The first time my soldier opened fire was by the village of Smonica on the 23rd of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So why do you record in this document an order that fire should be opened? Just explain to the Trial Chamber what the purpose of putting that in an order is if you don't intend it to occur.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am telling you that this is an order which is part of war games. I don't know how else to explain this to you. Coming from the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And nonetheless, the route that would be taken would be from the barracks at Djakovica up towards the area at the south of the lake. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that would have been the case had that been happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could just look briefly, please, at tab 9 for a moment. This is the 26th of April. Again, an order signed by Colonel Lazarevic, which is P1025 and annex 7 to your witness statement. Could I ask you just to look at paragraph 3.2 in that order, please, which in the English reads as follows: "The 3rd bVP is to perform in-depth security of the state border on the cross section right Koznjar border post to Decani. Left Kosare border post to Junik, with the following task: In cooperated action with the 53rd border battalion and the MUP forces prevent the violation of the border regime and ensure combat readiness for intervention along the axis of Decani-Junik to Smonica and Decani to Istinic village to Celopek village." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. I see what is written there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that -- was that war games as well or was that an intended deployment? For military purposes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, through war games the unit was brought to the border posts of Kosare and Morina to provide security at the state border.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that part of it. What I'm interested in is the combat readiness for intervention along the axis from Deqan to Istinic to Cellopek on the eastern side of the road by some very considerable distance. Can you help me with that, please. Was there, first of all, a planned deployment from Deqan across to Cellopek on the 26th of April?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, there was no planned deployment. I would like to note that the army units did not go east of the Pec-Djakovica road at all into the area of Dukagjin up until, I don't know what date, in July.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, we -- with the greatest of respect, Mr. Zivanovic, on your own evidence that cannot be right, because the 52nd Military Police Battalion at the very least was stationed in the area of the lake, was it not? Or at least, was positioned in the area of the lake. So it's --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Now, what I'm asking you to explain to the Trial Chamber, if you would, please, is what it means in this order that you have exhibited where combat readiness is required for intervention along an axis that goes from Deqani to Cellopek.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that the unit did not go along that route or it did not engage in any activity. It is true that the 52nd Battalion was in the area of Lake Radonjic, but I am not the superior officer of that unit. I am sorry, but you're asking me about professional comments in respect of orders issued by a superior. If you -- and I'm a witness here. Now, if you put me in a different position, then perhaps I will be able to say more.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, the position that you're in, Mr. Zivanovic, is as the officer in charge of the VJ forces in the area of responsibility to which this particular part of the order is directed. And I'm asking you to tell us what you understood by it. "Combat readiness for intervention along an axis from Deqan to Istinic to Cellopek." What did you understand that order to be requiring you to do, if anything?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we look at the entire situation that it was, namely that Combat Group 2 was in the area of Kramovik, then it was only logical to issue a task as an alternative task to another unit that is in Decani so that they could give support to Combat Group 2 if they are threatened in the ravine. You don't really think that a military unit is going to take a road where combat readiness is -- well, I mean, where there is full combat readiness and that they cannot open fire if they are in jeopardy.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand your answer. I'm simply asking you to explain what you thought you were being ordered to do, and you've given an explanation as far as it goes. Could you turn behind tab 10, please, for a moment. This is an order signed by you dated the 16th of May, 1998. This is Exhibit D70 and it's annex 29 to your 92 ter statement. And the first item in this order directs BG-2, Combat Group 2, to be at the ready in the current redeployment sector for operations along the following axes: From the barracks to Smonica village to Ponosevac village to Gornja Morina village, first of all. Secondly, from the barracks to Erecka Suka. And thirdly, from the barracks to Zrze village. And fourthly, from the barracks to Radonjic Lake. And the task that you have allocated to BG-2 reads: "In coordinated action with the neighbouring forces of the Republic of Serbia MUP, break up Siptar sabotage and terrorist groups and secure supply routes for VJ units." Now, pausing there for moment, can you help us, please. These deployments from the barracks in four different axes, would they be deployments from the barracks in Gjakova, where BG-2 was then based?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Combat Group 2 was in the barracks in Djakovica. However, these axes are not deployments. They are alternate routes for activity if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the activity that you're authorising is coordinated action with the MUP to break up the DTG and secure supply routes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I give an alternate route, then I also give a task. And a task is received in this way: If Group 52 is threatened in the area of Lake Radonjic, then the corps commander would issue an task to me to intervene in that area. Certainly there would be somebody else on that axis, not only me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. But it appears, does it not, to contemplate military engagements? Do I -- have I understood that correctly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right. How else could we operate if we already had terrorist activity?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, the first two of the axes that you've referred to here, from the barracks to Ponosevac and Gornja Morina, that is a deployment on the western side of the main road, but the remaining deployments from the barracks to Erecka Suka and the barracks to Zrze and the barracks to Radonjic Lake, those are deployments on the east side of the main road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that these are alternate routes. However, I am telling you that it is not deployment. These are possible alternate axes for use.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which one did they take or which ones did they take?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number one on the 23rd of May. This group went from the barracks to Smonica, Ponosevac, and Gornja Morina.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: BG-3 on this order is to be ready in the current redeployment sector for operations along axes from Pec-Decani-Rastavica-Junik-Ponosevac and from Pec to Zahac to Klina to Iglarevo and from Pec to Rausic to Barane to Celopek. Are you indicating that those are alternate axes as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Likewise, alternate routes, because they did not act along these axes. You see the task number 1 here is for them to link up with the combat group in Ponosevac. Combat Group 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you then delegate to the unit commanders, is that correct, how they are to interpret these orders?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They interpreted the way it was. They also issue alternate or alternative tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Who is it who chooses which of the three alternate routes they should take?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the level of command, who has order issuing authority. I was given my orders by the corps commander. Without his orders, I could not have used them along any axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so far as BG-3 is concerned, what was the axis taken on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a single one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. I want to turn, if I may, to the second half of May and ask you to look, please, at paragraphs 81 to 83 of your witness statement. Now, you describe in paragraph 82 an order from General Pavkovic forbidding movement along the Gjakova-Deqani road. And at paragraph 83, a joint VJ-MUP operation aimed at unblocking the main roads in the Mehotija area at the end of May. I just want to ask you some questions, please, if I may, about that phase of operations. We have heard that on the 25th of May there was a PJP sweep operation conducted involving the entering of villages on both sides of the main road following the disappearance of two PJP officers in the vicinity of Rastavica on the 23rd of May. Is that the joint operation that you are there referring to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. On the 23rd of May, I reached the village of Donja Morina. I'm not sure about this, because the Decani-Erec-Djakovica road was not used by the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you just to look, please, briefly behind tabs 11 and 12 in this bundle. Particularly behind tab 11. We have seen certain evidence that relates to an operation that took place in Ljubenic on the main road on the 25th of May in which a number of people were killed. And behind tab 12 - I don't ask that it be brought up on the screen - is a situation report from Colonel Crosland, who arrived in the area very shortly afterwards. The relevant documents, for the record, are D72, P6, page 23; and D71. Were you aware of an operation in Ljubenic at the end of May in which a number of civilians were killed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that, because I was dealing with the problems in the area of Morina.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if we could just have a look at tab 14, please, briefly, where Colonel Lazarevic decides on certain deployments on the 28th of May. And tab 14 is P1051 and is annex 35 to the 92 ter statement. If we look at the fourth bullet point in that document: "BG-3 of the 125th Motorised Brigade is ordered to lift the blockade of Pec -- of the Pec to Decani to Ljubenic road." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did that deployment occur?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I can't tell you this now. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How do you know it didn't occur?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the action didn't take place. Why, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, who decided to countermand this order? Was it you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The one who issued the order to begin with, Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And did he communicate that decision to you, as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are quite a few events that I can't really recall, and you keep insisting on the documents by my superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So when you say in paragraph 83 of your statement that a joint VJ-MUP operation aimed at unblocking the roads in the Metohija area took place at the end of May, that operation didn't include the carrying out by BG-3 of the order that's recorded here.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first day, on Thursday, I did not want to claim that some elements of the statements ought to be corrected, because -- this was not early May. This was end of July. It wasn't either early May or end of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, are you telling us that your 92 ter statement is wrong but you chose not to correct it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Why didn't you correct it when you noticed it was wrong?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was probably due to the time constraints. When I arrived here, there wasn't enough time. I had to prepare myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you notice any other errors?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several more. If we come across them, I'll draw your attention to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These errors are not significant ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's not, with respect, for you to judge. When you began your evidence, you were asked by Mr. Re whether if you were asked the same questions again you would give the same testimony as is recorded in your 92 ter statement. Do you remember that question?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember that, and that was the answer I gave.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you'd like to correct paragraph 83. Is it the position, then, that there wasn't in fact joint VJ and MUP operation attend of May to clear the main road? Is that the position? It didn't happen till July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in July.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, forgive me for suggesting this to you, but is it the position that you are in some difficulties in answering frankly to all of these questions because you know that you were not authorised to conduct joint operations with the MUP in anti-terrorist operations until late June?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, let's look back, please, at this document behind tab 14. Whether it happened or not, Colonel Lazarevic is ordering a coordinated action between the MUP and the VJ. Would you agree with that? Look at the first words, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Just look at the first words under "I have decided." It reads: "In coordination with MUP forces, lift the blockade of the Sisman Ponosevac-Molic-Junik and the Ponosevac-Donja Morina-Potok Molic roads." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you aware at the time in May that there was such a plan for joint operations with the MUP?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There existed a police station in the village of Ponosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you aware that orders were being issued by Colonel Lazarevic for joint MUP-VJ operations at the end of May?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand was I aware. I can see the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you read it at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if we just look, please, if we can, at the sixth bullet point. That orders the -- I'm sorry, the 2nd bVP to carry out a diversionary advance along the Radonjicka Jezero to Donji Bites village axis, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was -- this was also alternative task. If necessary, if a unit of the 52nd Battalion is in jeopardy, then this element should assist it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And assist it by conducting a diversionary advance? Could you explain for us, please, what that means in this context?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A diversionary attack. A "diversionary attack" means moving along the axes and displaying the force of one's unit with a view to reaching another one of its units.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did that occur?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, it's referred to in your witness statement at paragraph 84. Is that another of the areas where you noticed that you had recorded orders that did not in fact come -- become carried into effect? Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These orders contain alternate routes that could either not be used or were simply not used.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Could we look at tab 15, please, which is Exhibit D75, annex 46 to your 92 ter statement. And this one is dated the 23rd of June and orders the formation of temporary Combat Group number 5. And if we could just look, please, at paragraph 2. BG-5 is to be deployed to the Donji Bites village sector, Radonjicka Suka by 1500 hours on the 23rd of June, and in coordination with the 52nd Military Police Battalion and making use of Radonjicka Suka to prevent operations by the DTS along a series of axes, Rznic to Glodjane to Donji Bites to Gornji Ratis to Donji Ratis to Rakoc and Gramocelj to Donji Bites. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that. This is an order of Colonel Lazarevic asking that the group be set up. This has to do with what you asked me a couple of hours ago when you asked me about the red circle and what it meant. Well, this is the group.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was the group then deployed as described in this order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And we can see that that -- at paragraph 4 the order specifies that Radonjicka Cuka is to be taken over, as is a section of the features in Donji Bites by the Gjakova SUP units.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine. A record is taken of that so that something would not be recorded incorrectly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So just so that we understand the effect of this operation, that would be a MUP force going in first, would it? Followed by Combat Group 5?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It cannot be understood that way. MUP forces were already there at Cuka, and this area had to be taken over from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, then help us with that. Which MUP forces were already there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here precisely, there were forces from the Djakovica MUP, the regular forces from the town of Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And they were already in Donji Bites and on Radonjicka Cuka, were they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Radonjicka Cuka, but they were not in Donji Bites in the village itself. They were, rather, on a clearing near Bites.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And at this point BG-5 is deployed from -- we can see the route at paragraph 3 -- from Gjakova, if I can take it shortly, via Paljabarda to the village of Donji Bites; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only two small areas, and that's Cuka and this clearing or an -- or a plain on higher ground near Bites.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Okay. Do you notice the -- we obviously have at paragraph 1 the composition of Combat Group 5. Were the MUP forces evacuated at that point on their arrival, or did the MUP forces remain in that area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There remained only one MUP patrol at Cuka. The others were withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So from that point onwards, there would be a joint VJ and MUP operation based there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it seems. But these forces were not either planned for the operation or capable of seeing it through.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, could you explain that answer again, please. Just explain what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only on one place. If you can see Combat Group 5 was supposed to replace the men from the 52 -- 52nd Battalion in the area of the filtration plant.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. You told us, I think, a moment ago that going back to Mr. Delic's map this deployment reflects the broken line around Radonjicka Cuka. Is that a correct understanding of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I have a look at the map again? I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Behind tab 1. And the order is, to remind you, behind tab 15: "Deploy BG-5 to the Donji Bites village sector, Radonjicka Cuka." The first map behind tab 1. I think -- Witness, it's even further forward than that. There it is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. This is Recka Cuka [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We are to understand that those forces were based there from the 23rd of June. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And finally on this topic - and just before I suggest a break --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness says this is Recka Cuka. That's not entirely clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Let me clarify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You have the map in front of you on the screen. We can see the flag with the figure "6" upon it and a broken circle around Erecka Suka. I'm sorry, it's my mistake. Around Radonjicka Cuka and Donji Bites. Is that the location that you're referring to? Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Erecka Suka is a dominant feature and a very important one. Whoever had it under their control would control the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, let's -- we need to be absolutely clear about this, because Erecka Suka is a hill close to the village of Baballoq, near to the main road. Radonjicka Cuka is the hill which we see both on the map and in the order that we have just looked at, adjacent to the village of Donji Bites. You can see on the map the deployment and the broken line is around Radonjicka Cuka and Donji Bites. And in the document behind tab 15, the deployment of BG-5 is to Donji Bites, Radonjicka Cuka, making use of Radonjicka Cuka to prevent DTS operations. So to be absolutely clear, it is Radonjicka Cuka that is referred to here.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right. You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally, if I may, before moving to another subject, could you please look behind tab 16 for a moment. Tab 16 is Exhibit D83 and annex 66 to the 92 ter statement. If you could just look briefly, please, at paragraph 3.9. This is an order from General Pavkovic dated the 18th of August. And at paragraph 3.9, it orders the withdrawal of the 52nd bVP from Radonjicko Jezero to the Kosovski Junaci barracks and the transfer the positions to the MUP forces. Now, first of all, 52nd bVP is translated here as "bomber regiment." Do you understand the 52nd bVP to be the Military Police Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Military Police Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So would you agree this order of the 18th of August is directing the withdrawal of the Military Police Battalion and its replacement by MUP forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did that occur?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And what MUP forces were they, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say here, so I can't tell you really. I suppose PJPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would that be a suitable moment to take the next break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It certainly would. We'll have a break until five minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, I want to ask you some questions about the evidence you've given in relation to MUP patrols during 1998 and the information that came to you about what they had discovered. Last Thursday you testified that during the first half of 1998, between the 28th of February, when the incident at Likoshan occurred, and the middle of the year, MUP patrols in the area to the east of the main road would come across evidence of KLA military training, and you said that that was something that occurred all the way down from Prapacan via Isniq, Dashinoc, and Gllogjan. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And how frequently would you receive information of that kind from the MUP during the first half of 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two or three pieces of information on the whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In -- in the six-month period?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You have specific recollection, then, of such patrols reporting back from the areas of Dashinoc and Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, because there were so few of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you also said that during the second half of 1998, from June onwards, MUP forces found medical materials while conducting searches or tracking down terrorists in different villages. Can you give us a sense, please, of how frequently you would hear of MUP patrols conducting searches or tracking down terrorists in the villages to the east of the main road.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And I wonder if you could just look for us briefly at tab 17 in the bundle, which is Exhibit P1046 and annex 30 to your statement. Do you have it? Tab 17.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Now, this is a document signed by you dated the 20th of May and addressed to the Pristina Corps command and is described as a regular combat report. Can I understand this is you reporting to the overall corps command in Pristina and seeking both to inform them and to receive instructions from them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was duty-bound to report to them every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. If we could just look, please, at the penultimate bullet point, which should be, I think, in your copy the -- the B/C/S version, the last bullet point on the first page and in the English translation, the third bullet point on the second page. It reads: "MUP forces are currently carrying out a serious operation in the sector of the villages of Gornja Grabanica, Dolovo, Ceskovo, and Kpuz. They want to know whether VJ units would be able to support them if need be. They are deploying their mortars in the Donje Cuprevo village sector." Now, in reporting this request to the corps command, are you seeking instructions as to whether or not VJ units would be able to support the MUP if need be?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This only has to do with information that they were asking for that, but I did not explicitly ask for approval as to whether I should give support or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But just to be clear, on the 20th of May you could not have lawfully given support to that operation, could you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. No, I am sorry -- according to the law -- well, no, without an order issued by the corps commander. He is the law for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that, but you've told us, have you not, that it wasn't until the end of June that the VJ was given authorisation to conduct joint operations with the MUP against the KLA? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Are you not here conveying to the corps command a request specifically to put your own units at the disposal of the MUP if need be?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said "no." I was not explicit in asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to summarise, if I may, to you four key points to have emerged from the overall testimony of Colonel Crosland, who, as you may or may not be aware, was visiting your area of responsibility and bordering areas of the 549th throughout 1998. First of all, he has testified that during 1998 and 1999 he personally saw between 200 and 300 villages burnt with crops wantonly burned by Serb forces, businesses of all sorts, petrol stations, shops looted within towns like Decani, Pec, and Gjakova. He testified that he had observed VJ as well as SAJ, PJP, JSO, and others, engaging in this destruction. And that he saw animals shot and crops and animal feed stacks being burned and deliberately destroyed. So that's the first overall heading. And the references for that are 3058 to 3060. Secondly -- I'm putting these four points to you because I'm going to give you an opportunity to comment on them. Secondly, he testified that the British ambassador on the basis of his reports conveyed to President Milosevic the British government's assessment that the military campaign over the summer of 1998, in which your forces participated, amounted to the commission of crimes against humanity and amounted to a widespread and systematic campaign against the Albanian civilian population. That's page 3061. Thirdly, he has testified that the role of the VJ was to provide long-range shelling cover for these operations; that there would be a destructive phase of bombardment of a village by the VJ from a distance and that paramilitary police formations would then enter the village and conduct burning operations. And fourthly, that the VJ forces that were involved in those actions were the forces commanded by General Bozidar Delic of the 549th and by yourself, of the 125th and that, in his opinion, the involvement of your forces in those operations could not have occurred without your authority. And the reference for that is 3063 to 3068. I'm going to invite you, first of all, to comment on that series of allegations overall, if you wish to.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the allegation made that we were torching, destroying, looting, damaging, and I don't know what all the expressions used were, I claim that only if there were a building that was a target, where a terrorist had been or where fire had been opened from, that is the only kind of building that would have been targeted. And how should I put this? It would be checked. Furthermore, it is possible, due to the use of different kinds of ammunition, that there can be a fire. So the -- so it appears that it is intentional. Also, every third or fourth bullet could be an incendiary one. We strictly got orders not to allow soldiers to enter and take other people's things, as we say; that is to say, to loot. If we caught anyone, if we observed any such thing, we would bring such a person into custody or take disciplinary measures. Further on, as for Metohija, our two units, Bozidar Delic's and mine, were deployed there but we did not do anything that constituted a violation of international humanitarian law. Over 200 villages burnt? I'm not aware of that. I know that over 200 villages were in the Pec district and were cleansed of Serbs and Montenegrins. That would be it. I don't know whether there's anything else that I have not commented upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you for that. I then want to ask you, please, in the light of those answers about some specific documents to see if you can help us with them. Could you look behind tab 18, please. Tab 18 is Exhibit P -- or marked for identification as P1053 and is annex 38 to your statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, before we continue, has the witness commented on all the things you said, especially the last one, that the -- such operations, even if they have not taken place, could not have occurred without the authority? Was your control such that such things could have happened without you knowing it? And when I say "such things," I'm talking about the crimes allegedly committed: Looting, burning, cattle being shot. Could you imagine, was your control such that you'd say, "No, no, if that would have happened, I would have known"? Because that was the last comment, I think, by Colonel Crosland.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for killings and persecutions, I would have known about that. As for looting, I cannot say anything with 100-degree certainty. But when we would review our units, after having carried out activities, if we would find anything on a particular soldier, then we would hold that soldier accountable or we would send an appropriate document to the military court in Nis in order to have criminal charges brought against such a person. I haven't got any of this here with me now, but we handed over quite a bit of material to judiciary organs for them to deal with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give an estimate about -- about how many persons? Are we talking about tens of -- or hundreds or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can. It's tens. And it primarily pertains to the later part; that is to say, on the eve of the aggression. And in these actions, it is up to ten; in 1998, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Do you mean 1998? Because I think the whole question was referring to general statements, meaning 1998 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: This is what -- how you formulated it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think what the witness has just indicated it that there were up to ten criminal reports filed during 1999 -- I'm sorry, during 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And tens filed in the run-up to the NATO military action in 1999. That's as I understood his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we could ask you. You said "approximately ten or up to ten in 1998." And the total number including 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for 1998, up to ten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes and for 1999? Could you give us an estimate? You said it was more than?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as my unit is concerned, about 20. I cannot tell you exactly whether it was, say, 19 or 23. I cannot tell you exactly now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do you know whether sending in such a report ever led to prosecution of those you at that time reported to be responsible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, particularly higher-ranking officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But no soldiers on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand that. An officer would be punished with a year in prison. That kind of term, for instance. And a soldier would not be punished then but once he completed his military service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want just to look very briefly with you, please, at a number of orders at around this period of time. Could you look, then, at tab 18. I think I've put the references on the record. This is an order dated the 30th of May and signed by Major General Pavkovic. And at item number 4, he orders as follows: "Provide support to MUP units from the units' deployment area, using combat equipment from a distance, in accordance with their characteristics." Now, this obviously predates the authorisation for the VJ to act jointly with the MUP in anti-terrorist operations, does it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was issued, but it has to do with the decision-making powers of the corps commander. It does not have to mean that this was actually carried through.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. But it was an order that you saw at the time, was it? It's addressed to the 125th, for example.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So I want to understand, then, what you understood at the time by an order to provide support using combat equipment from a distance. What -- what do you understand by the expression "using combat equipment from a distance"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding of that was in the spirit of the last sentence; that is to say: "Provide support only in accordance with the decision of the commander." Support "from a distance" means primarily by using artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so just so that we're clear, on the face of this order, Major General Pavkovic is directing, is he not, a state of affairs where VJ forces could be used to provide long-range artillery support for MUP operations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Those are the kind of tasks he is issuing. I don't know whether he was ordered by someone else to do that. I don't know and I'm not going to interfere in terms of his competency.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you saw this order at the time, did you not think that it was inconsistent with the constitutional role you understood the VJ to be performing at that time, which was confined to the area to the east of the main road involved in border operations alone?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Over here it is not stated specifically what the area in question is; however, it can be assumed that the MUP can be supported within a 5-kilometre belt.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that's how it would have been understood. Could we look at tab 19, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, before we continue. Could you tell us who the commander of all forces in Kosovo and Metohija refers to. It says: "Provide support only at the request of the commander of all forces in Kosovo and Metohija according to my decision." Who is that, "commander of all forces"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The commander of the Pristina Corps is Major General Pavkovic at this point in time, and he is referring to his own overall forces. And it says down here "to," and it is actually all the units of the Pristina Corps. You see underneath the signature all the units that this was sent to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But what I do not understand - but please help me - why doesn't he say provide support only if I give specific orders? Or is that just a linguistic ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I assume that General Pavkovic had received a request from the very top that it is possible to provide such support and that he should be ready in that sense, and he issued this then as a preparatory order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would -- if you say "the top," is that the political top?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not political. I am only talking about the military top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's why I'm -- since in this paragraph here talking about MUP and about the military, because the military is expected to provide support to the MUP; therefore, the language "all forces" has ... So that's not military and police forces together? Because I was then wondering who was in command of those forces together, taken together.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I? The commander of the military forces is General Pavkovic in Kosovo and Metohija. Above him is the commander of the 3rd Army, who was in Nis together with his command. And in part there was the forward command post in Pristina. General Pavkovic and we, at the lower levels, were never in a position to command the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I have to understand that "commander of all forces" refers to the superior to Pavkovic -- to General Pavkovic? Military superior.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it can be put that way too, but it was my understanding that he was the commander of the overall military forces in Kosovo and Metohija within the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we just look, please, if we may, behind tab 19 which is Exhibit P1055 and annex 40 to your statement. This is a 1st of June direction by Major General Pavkovic. And I'm interested, please, in the text that appears in the B/C/S version as the last three lines in paragraph 5 on page 2. And in the English version in the last three lines, again, of paragraph 5 appearing on page 2. It reads: "With a tank platoon of the 125th Motorised Brigade BG-3, provide assistance to MUP forces along the Crnobreg-Prilep village road in crushing strong resistance points on the line of attack." Now, first of all, this also is an order that predates the authorisation to engage the VJ in anti-terrorist operations, is it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is an order that precedes it. And if you look at who it was sent to, it is not a classical order. It is addressed to the commander of the 3rd Army, General Pavkovic's superior; that is to say, for his information. And if he approves of it, then it will be carried through.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And do I understand the evidence you gave last Thursday to be this: That where Major General Pavkovic speaks about a tank platoon providing assistance to the MUP in crushing strong resistance points on the line of attack, that the role of the tank platoon was purely for psychological support?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the way it was supposed to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, do you know whether that's the way it was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that did actually happen, that the tank did not fire a single projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we look behind tab 20 for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can I ask one additional question. Mr. -- Mr. Zivanovic, your answer here again is that "if he approves of it, then it will be carried through." You always leave open whether such coordinated action actually took place, yes or no, or whether it was just ordered but not ... Is -- is that your testimony, that you are not aware that this actually happened or is it -- or do you say yes, yes, of course we -- on his orders, on General Pavkovic's orders, we -- we did such coordinated actions? Because you make a reservation there that...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. You have to understand me. I really would like you to understand me. I'm a soldier. That is to say, that I cannot do anything on my own. If I do something that way, then I have to explain very well to my superior what I did. You noticed this right. There are quite a few orders that say "engage along the axis," et cetera. That is to say, this is an alternate task. When something is done, then there is a report, a specific one. And that is why it seems that I have reservations. That's the way it looks to you. I cannot claim anything that had not been done. Do you understand what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. But then quite a simple question is: Were such -- did such coordinated actions finally take place or did they -- were they ordered several times and did they never take place? I'm just trying to find out what -- what actually happened. I mean, if you give a military order, it's not uncommon that such an order finally is -- is -- is followed by the subordinates. Now, you say again and again "if he would approve," then so-and-so. I'm now asking you: Were such coordinated actions approved, did they actually take place, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Activities in the roads, Smonica, Ponosevac, Batusa, Kosare. There was cooperation between the MUP and my unit or the battalion that was providing security at the border. As the cooperation referred to here as alternate tasks, that was carried out as well by way of psychological support to the MUP forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm turning now to tab -- bear with me just one moment -- tab 20, which is Exhibit P1063 and annex 49 to the statement. Mr. Zivanovic, we're now in July. This is an order of the 17th of July signed by yourself. And it refers to a planned operation which we see in paragraph 1 is to take place between the 17th and the 20th of July involving active operations from a distance on a daily basis aimed at exposed terrorist forces in the area of responsibility which are engaged in attacks on the VJ units located in the field and on the road communications, and so on. First of all, did -- do you remember this order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were these operations carried out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In part. When I say "in part," I mean -- well, if you wish, we can have a look at this part of the plan. This is an integral part of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm -- I'm going to look at the targets in a moment with you. If we can just pick up some of the details of the report. At paragraph 3, there is a reference to "ensuring only targets outside of populated areas." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Paragraph 5, I just wanted to seek your assistance with that. The second sentence suggests that troops should carry out these operations without displaying unit or VJ insignia. Was there a particular reason for that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. You know, when an operative of mine drafts an order, I sign it even if there are some errors if they don't really go against the implementation of the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And at 6: "Operations are not to be carried out in the areas where representatives of embassies and consulates, journalists, observers and representatives of humanitarian organisations, regardless of the activities and intensity of the terrorist forces." Can I ask you, was there a particular reason why you would choose not to conduct activities where they might be seen by international observers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to activities from a distance upon terrorist forces. The problem here was that I -- we didn't have anyone who could provide us with the information as to the exact positions of the terrorist forces, and we prepared this with reservations. Of course, we were given the following assignment: Should a diplomatic representative or anybody else bearing the insignia of -- of the UNHCR be present there and if there is terrorist activity, regardless of our possible losses, we should not open fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm just seeking a slight clarification. It's at page 85, line 6. In the document at paragraph 3, one word is illegible. Mr. Emmerson read onto the record the word "ensuring." It says: "In the course of operations, only/illegible/targets outside of population areas -- populated areas." I'm just asking if Mr. Emmerson has understood the word in Serbian to be "ensuring" or if not perhaps the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could read the document and tell us what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I was paraphrasing and summarising. There's a photocopy blip on the original. But maybe the witness can read paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We could ask him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Item 3? I can't make this out now. I'm trying to put this into context. I think that it says: "In the course of activity exclusively to spell out or" -- I can't really make this out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we can't --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't read it either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can't expect you to read the illegible. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we look, please, then, at the attached list of targets, and in particular at item number 3 on the list in the context of the injunction to avoid populated areas. We can see that -- that the target there is listed as a school in Orahovo village. Can you help us with that at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. This relates to school holidays, so the schools are closed. Second, information was received of the possible presence of terrorists there. And, third, I can only see the objective under number 1, to fire from a distance because the Stari Trg repeater came under fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that. But -- it may have been school holidays, presumably the schoolchildren would have been at their homes in the village.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But if terrorists are present in the school building, then this can be regarded as their barracks and as an appropriate target.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you would then fire at that from a distance using long-range artillery. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I had had reliable information about terrorists being present there, I would have fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is that target consistent with the order to target -- seek targets outside of populated areas, in your view?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But wherever there are terrorists present, that is a target.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I see. Tab 20A, which is the list of targets is Exhibit P1064 and is annex 50 to the witness's 92 ter statement. Can we have a look at tab 21 now, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me ask one additional question. Mr. Zivanovic, what Mr. Emmerson apparently is asking you is why target a school, even if there are terrorists in that school, with a weapon from a long distance, a 120-millimetre mortar, at least as far as I'm aware of, is not a weapon that you fire from close range. And he didn't say it, but isn't the mortar considered to be an area weapon rather than a weapon which attacks very precise targets, that is, in -- within 10, 20 metres? That's, I think, the question Mr. Emmerson is putting to you. Correct me if I'm wrong, but schools often are in villages in populated areas. Of course, you have also schools outside of villages. I don't know whether you have any specific knowledge about this school, but if -- if it is a school just in the middle of a village. Then the question of Mr. Emmerson is: Why target such a school with a 120-millimetre mortar?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only because of the target. I said, if terrorists are present there, then that is a military target. I really can't say where the school building in question is, whether it's on the edge of the village or in the centre of the village. The 120-millimetre mortar is an appropriate weapon for that, regardless of your opinion. You thought that it could not hit the target spot on, but it can, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not saying it can't hit it. That is not what I said. I gave you an opportunity to comment on a question I think Mr. Emmerson put to you and when he mentioned the mortar, that's what I thought he had in mind. So by making this more explicit, I gave you an opportunity to -- to comment on that. But I've heard your answer. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we turn now, please, to tab 21, which is Exhibit P1007, and it's annex 67 to this witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is an order dated the 19th of August signed by you and addressed to the commanders of Combat Groups 1, 2, 3, and 4. I just want to ask you about two matters, please, if I may. After the specific deployments of the combat groups that are there set out, on -- the -- just about halfway down the first page of text in the B/C/S and at the very bottom of the first page of text in the English, there is a paragraph that reads: "Exercise complete combat control of the area abandoned by the sabotage and terrorist forces, put into effect complete control, take security measures against all kinds of surprises, and preclude any kind of infiltration by the sabotage and terrorist groups." Can I understand, please: This obviously is an order issued after the offensive that you have drawn for us on the map of the 11th and 12th of August. This is issued about a week after that. Can you help us as to the areas that you are there referring to as the areas abandoned by the sabotage and terrorist forces over which complete control is to be established?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Combat Group 1 was in the area of the hunting rifle ammunition in Srbica at the time, which is in the area of Drenica. Combat Group 2 was above Junik from the village of Jasic toward the Zar Kolibe, by the border. Combat Group 3 was on the firing range at Belo Polje, which is our training grounds. And Combat Group 4 was at the Kosovska Mitrovica barracks. The tasks relate to these axes, to these routes that I mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you, please, just to explain to us that the concluding words of this order, which in the B/C/S will be the last two lines above the letters "JV" and in the English read as follows: "I disallow any subsequent activities of the units in the areas of villages and on the axes where media representatives carry out their activities." What -- what in that context do you mean by "subsequent activities" that you're disallowing in this particular order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had problems with the way in which the anti-terrorist combat was portrayed in the media. The aspirations of the terrorists was to internationalise the conflict and we were not really convinced that the events were reported about in a proper way by all. I said therefore -- I ordered that we should not open fire if there are representatives of the mass media present, even at the cost of the terrorists possibly spilling over from one area to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you just turn, please, to tab 28 in the bundle for a moment. This is an extract from the minutes of the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija for the 7th of August, so 12 days before this order that you have -- you have issued. And is there is an entry there against the name of Mr. Sainovic which reads: "The greatest damage to us is caused by burning the houses without any need, which could cause pressures to the country." Do you see that entry?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but under what item is that? What bullet is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's the second bullet point under the heading of Mr. Sainovic's name.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And, for the record, that is D85, page 46 in the English translation. Were you aware that at the political level concern was being expressed that houses were being unnecessarily burnt in the summer operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I allow for the possibility of such cases existing. But as I said a moment ago, as part of the army, I tried to sanction this whenever I learnt of this. And I would have an additional explanation concerning the Joint Command, if you deem it helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you any questions about it. Mr. Re can ask them to you if he wishes to in re-examination, unless the Trial Chamber wishes me to seek the clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber does not encourage you to further go in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want, if I may now, please, to ask you, in the context of the answers that you've given, some very specific questions about deployments that you ordered on the 23rd and 24th of July. And for this, you will need to look behind tab 1C. And it might be of assistance if you were to take out the map that appears behind tab 1C and to have it available to you. Do you have the map available, Mr. Zivanovic? Behind tab 1C is a map that looks like this. It's -- it's Exhibit D105. Can I suggest, Mr. Zivanovic, that you take the map out of the bundle and have it available to you beside the remainder of the documents.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we can just put that map to one side. If we can please look behind tab 23, which is Exhibit P1065 and annex 51 to your witness statement. Now, this is an order dated the 23rd of July and signed by you. And we can see that at paragraph 2 of the order you order the commander of BG-3 to deploy part of their forces, a tank platoon, to support active operations of the PJP, 6th and 7th Detachment, aimed at clearing and unblocking the road communications on the axis Dolac village, Kukavica, Iglarevo, Stepenice to Kijevo. If we can just look at the map for a moment. At the time of this deployment, where would they have started from, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first action that was carried out as part of the joint action at the end of July. The forces of Combat Group 3, the tank platoon, would set out from the area when you cross the bridge at the juncture to Klina and Djakovica, along the Pec-Pristina road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we can just plot the route that you have ordered them to take. Just south on our map of Klina, we see, I think, the village of Dolac; is that correct? Your glasses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we perhaps also have the exhibit in e-court so that we can more easily zoom in and -- because it is an existing exhibit, from --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think it is the -- it's certainly on my screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, it is -- oh, I'm -- yes. But then we could perhaps zoom in --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see, for the witness's assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I was pushing the wrong button.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We'll move -- we'll need to move up the map some -- a little further, please. And then -- and then heading -- heading in the opposite direction; in other words, show a portion of territory further west until we see Klina. I'm afraid we're on the wrong part of the map at the moment. We need to move --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think we have to move it north. If the map is in its totality in e-court, there should be a possibility to -- if we move up north.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think -- I think it's possible, looking at the area that's sectioned in e-court, but there may be a technical error with the scanning, so we may need to work from the paper copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's move --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Perhaps we can work with paper for the moment, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You can see -- just so that we can see the axis, please. Just south of Klina, do you see the village of Dolac? It's south and very slightly to the east.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just there. Exactly so. And if we just travel -- if we travel in an easterly direction along that road, do we then come to the village of Iglarevo, and following Iglarevo in the same direction, we come to the village of Kijevo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we just look back to the order, we can see that item number 5, you have ordered BG-2 to block the village of Junik and to support activities of the PJP aimed at mopping up Siptar gangs in the village of Junik. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And then at item 6, if I can paraphrase it this way, the -- the order is for the BG-3 commander together with the commanders of the 6th and the 7th Detachments of the PJP to conduct reconnaissance along the axis we've just looked at and also along the axis from Pec to Decane to Junik. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just, if I can on this dual operation, to be absolutely clear. If we look behind tab 24, there's a further order for the following day. Tab 24 is Exhibit P01 -- I'm sorry, P066, and it's annex 52. I won't go through the details of it, but can you look, please, at the first and second paragraphs of that order and do they confirm that the manoeuvres set out in the order of the 23rd of July should be carried into effect?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the first bullet point was carried out. Combat Group 3 had one tank platoon. One went to Krgjalevo [as interpreted], the other one to Junik. Junik was -- or had been blocked for a longer while at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And -- and the second paragraph deals with the deployment towards the village of Iglarevo and then towards Kijevo, does it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. The second paragraph reads: "Provide support to the MUP forces in the liberation of Kijevo." Because Kijevo had been blocked by the Siptar forces and that was where the MUP was deployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, if you could turn, please, behind tab 25, which is -- needs to be not shown on the screen, because it is a situation report produced by Colonel Crosland about which he has given some oral evidence. This is a situation report, and it's D78 as an exhibit - filed by Colonel Crosland on the 30th of July concerning a tour of duty in this area on the 28th and 29th of July. And you can see in the summary, having toured the area, he concludes in the last line of that summary: "How do Serb authorities explain wanton damage to towns and villages." I wonder if I may, with the benefit of the map in the few minutes that remain, just to go through the route that he took. You can see that he began in -- under detail 1, he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I am afraid that three minutes might not be enough, since I would need two minutes as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, it might be better to start this part of the exercise, if I may, tomorrow. And I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's do that. And perhaps you could also provide -- because there's now some discrepancy between the map we find in our binders and the map which is in e-court to the extent it can be manipulated in e-court. It seems like it's a more limited map in e-court. So if you would take care of that as well. Then we have a late start tomorrow. And perhaps I'll already allow you, Mr. Zivanovic, to leave the courtroom but not until I've instructed you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony whether already given or still to be given.
