I would like to see you back tomorrow at quarter past 4.00 in the afternoon. Then, Madam Usher, could you escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to know how much time is further needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I will certainly conclude cross-examination within the -- the hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Within the hour. So if we start tomorrow at 4.15, that would bring us to 5.15. I'm looking at other counsel. Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Half an hour to 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Half an hour to 45 minutes. Let's keep on the safe side. That brings us to 5.45, then a break, and then after the break another 50 minutes brings us to 6.30. Yes, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I will need at least half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Half an hour. That would bring us to 7.00 tomorrow. Mr. Re --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, I must emphasise "at least."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Half an hour to 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we will stop anyhow at 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I know you will stop at 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, I'm not only asking in relation to this witness -- Mr. Re. But also in relation to the remainder of the programme this week, because we have -- we have Professor Aleksandric and another witness scheduled for this week. We are not sitting on Thursday, as you may have noticed. Could you tell us how much time would still be needed for Professor Aleksandric? That's -- and how much time would the witness still on the list take?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The witness still on the list, we've managed to get -- to come -- I've sent an e-mail to Chambers saying that she was coming tomorrow morning, hopefully to testify tomorrow afternoon. I -- our estimate is about 45 minutes. In relation to Professor Aleksandric, I'd have to speak to Mr. Dutertre, who's not here today. I think about half an hour or so. I think. Given that it's -- the main issue left over was in relation to Professor Lecomte and Mr. Dourel's report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And for Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In terms of the lay witness, if I can use that expression.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I at the moment can't envisage having very much, if anything, for her. As far as Professor Aleksandric is concerned, I'm reviewing my notes in that regard. Obviously, I will need to deal with the issue as between himself and Professor Lecomte and one or two other matters, and I would have thought somewhere in the region of one and a half hours. He, of course, hasn't been cross-examined at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And other counsel, for Professor Aleksandric and the lay witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the lay witness, I think there will be virtually no examination whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't hear you very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the lay witness, there will be virtually no examination whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to Professor Aleksandric, it's really going to depend on the state of play after direct and the cross prior to mine, but I don't think it will be terribly long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That answer is fully correct and doesn't help me entirely out. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm somewhat -- I'm somewhat dependent on my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not -- I'm not blaming you for it but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In the spirit of helpfulness, I think I will be 10 to 15 minutes with the lay witness at most, and I am reasonably confident that after Mr. Emmerson I am not likely to have many, if any, questions for -- for Professor Aleksandric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I then would very much encourage the parties to see that tomorrow in the short session that we would deal with the present witness and to see whether we can make the further examination as efficient as possible so in order to ... That means that if you'd use all of the time you indicated now, that we might not manage to do that. If you all could save 10 per cent, 12/13 per cent, there's a fair chance that it would steal some time for Mr. Re in re-examination as well. Yes, I see you, Mr. Re, you are nodding "yes." You see, I thought about you already.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, it's not really icing on the cake. It's part of the process if we need to clarify something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's see how far we can come tomorrow, because for Wednesday then, I think that the lay witness and Professor Aleksandric together should be possible to -- to finalise their examination, especially if -- if someone would have to wait, then, for another -- if we can't sit on Thursday, then to wait for another Thursday -- do we have to explore the possibility of sitting on Friday? That's, of course, usually not scheduled. We'll give that some thought and we'll see what would be the best to do. At this moment, I cannot announce anything else. Then we'll adjourn until tomorrow, 4.15 in Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 16th day of October, 2007, at 4.15 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
